# Cloud and cloud-callout native controls

Original fixture generated by `tools/cloud_callout_fixture.py` from the project's
independently authored shape-defaults package. No corpus artwork is embedded.
Eight shapes isolate cloud, default cloudCallout, diagonal callout positions,
and four cardinal positions on tall shapes. The top four shapes are wide.
The manifest records preset adjustments and physical dimensions.

The reference application exported the one-page reference read-only. The full page was
visually inspected; the cloud stretches with the shape, while callout bubbles
remain circular and can extend beyond its rectangle. Source and PDF hashes are
recorded in reference.json. The source passes the repository's OOXML schema
validator with exit zero. This fixture is a native reference, not a claim of
pixel identity between different rasterizers.

The supplied ECMA-376 Part 1 DrawingML geometry definitions describe cloud and
cloudCallout in OfficeOpenXML-DrawingMLGeometries/presetShapeDefinitions.xml.
Their paths use elliptical arcTo commands; cloudCallout additionally uses two
adjustments and three circular subpaths. Both presets now import using original
geometry code. The custom-path branch still does not support arbitrary arcTo.
The final native/browser page pair was inspected. Automated browser comparisons
cover all eight shapes through edit, undo and reopen, excluding the heading's
unrelated font fallback. They permit one pixel of antialiasing displacement,
48/255 channel difference and fewer than 0.5% unmatched sampled ink pixels.
This covers body outlines, interior strokes and circular bubbles outside the
shape bounds. Native PDF operators establish fill-all-then-stroke-all order,
which matters for overlapping default bubbles. No reference/spec divergence is
established. Text bounds follow the preset equations; native cloud text and
degenerate callout positions need separate calibration.

`tools/record_cloud_callouts.py` renders the retained PDF at four pixels/point
then downsamples with BOX to 96 DPI, recording its PNG hash with source/PDF hashes.
